newsitem.title: USA: CBOT members vote to amend LIFFE linkage agreement.
newsitem.headline: CBOT members vote to amend LIFFE linkage agreement.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade said Tuesday its members voted to amend an agreement with the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange on trading each other's products.

The proposal "to remove restrictions on exchanges' use of their respective off-hours electronic trading systems and to provide for remedies if inequitable volume levels develop through the link" was passed by a margin of 375-1/6 to 62-5/6, CBOT said in a recorded announcement.
Full CBOT members had one full vote each while associate members had 1/6 of a vote.

Under the new plan, CBOT's U.S. Treasury bond derivatives trading on the exchange's Project A electronic system would overlap with LIFFE's open-outcry trading in CBOT T-bond contracts, which is due to start on May 9.

In return, LIFFE would be able to trade its German Bund futures and options and other leading European contracts on its APT electronic system to overlap with CBOT's floor session, which also starts on May 9.

When CBOT board of directors came up with the plan late in January on the back of a remarkable growth in Project A volume, it stirred concerns that Project A could sap liquidity away from LIFFE T-bond trading and that the start of the CBOT-LIFFE linkage could be delayed.

Days after the plan surfaced, CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor and LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth, who were together at an industry conference in Arizona, downplayed such concerns, stressing the strategic importance of the open-outcry linkage.
